look_here_first: BARNYARDGRASS: look first at a clean and intact grass BLADE–SHEATH junction: there is NO true ligule (neither projecting membrane nor fringe) and NO auricles. Our new licensed Harry Rose photo demonstrates this negative character, absent from older gallery. Next trace the crowded flowering panicle and its side branches; find mature true spikelets (typically 2.5–4 mm) with variable lower sterile-lemma awns. The new real author-labelled spikelet photograph teaches multiple florets as botanically distinct from separate spikelets. IMPORTANT: native E. muricata shares the absent ligule; never identify introduced E. crus-galli from a distant head alone. To distinguish it, examine the abruptly delimited thin terminal margin and short hair line on the mature upper fertile lemma at ~25–40x.

morphology_keys.life_cycle: Annual, warm-season grass, often stout 0.3–1.2 m in Texas descriptions; grows in moist/disturbed soil, ditches, trails and edges.
best_field_traits: ABSENT leaf ligule and auricles; hair at nearby collar cannot substitute.
Smooth/glabrous sheaths, rather broad flat blades with pale conspicuous midvein; lower stem may be reddish.
Branching often erect to nodding terminal panicle with dense clusters of spikelets; flowering branch rachis frequently rough or bristly.
Spikelets around 2.5–4 mm long; lower fertile structures may be awnless or awned, even varying along one branch.
Mature upper fertile lemma hard body abruptly separated from thin membranous tip by line of minute hairs; inspect at ~25×.
crew_field_check: LOOK AT COLLAR: confirm no true ligule or auricles (not shown by original stored picture).
LOOK AT PANICLE: find branching axis and compact clustered spikelets (original photo markers show these).
LOOK UNDER MICROSCOPE: where E. muricata is possible, identify the abrupt membranous fertile lemma tip and line of minute hairs; if invisible leave Echinochloa sp.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: High resolution true collar close-up showing a blade/sheath junction without projecting ligule or auricles; include millimeter reference.
Whole robust plant including lower reddish/green sheaths and basal rooted tuft.
One mature spikelet beside 1-mm ruler, glumes and variable lower sterile-lemma awns visible.
25–40× comparison of mature fertile upper lemma TIP and line of minute hairs of E. crus-galli versus E. muricata; include palea tip.
Rachis node macro of bristle-like hairs with clear anatomical scale; NOT a substitute for final species call.
Actually inspect all external photos before selecting additional arrows; archive rights-clean files if accepted for public gallery.
diagnostic_photo_sequence_20261022: 1. START at whole plant: inspect source-labelled rooted rosette/young shoot (prior Polish photo) and mature stand (previous Maui photo).
2. Show TRUE leaf collar, at blade/sheath junction (Harry Rose 'ligule1'): no projecting flap nor hairy ligule. Absence must be proven on intact clean leaf; adjacent sparse hairs are not a ligule.
3. Follow full terminal PANICLE from main axis into lateral spikelet-rich branches. Existing locally stored Mark Marathon photo has three actually reviewed broad arrows.
4. Look at actual lower sterile lemma awn variability (Matt Lavin photo). Awn length is NOT sole species separator within Echinochloa.
5. Inspect true spikelet anatomy in original author-annotated Harry Rose actual macro (2-flowered, usually 2.5–4 mm in treatment). The body of one spikelet is NOT one panicle branch.
6. Inspect mature spikelets in second Harry Rose image; identify mature fertile upper lemma and lower sterile units, though individual pixel labels beyond source not asserted.

7. Compare DIFFERENT SPECIES Digitaria ciliaris photo: its flowering branches are fingers with paired one-flowered units and the plant has an actual membranous ligule (not visible in this comparison photo).

8. Escalate E. crus-galli versus native E. muricata candidates to macro: photograph several attached ripe upper fertile lemmas with basal body and thin distal tip, documenting a real line of minute hairs with 0.5–1 mm bar at 25–40x. If unresolved, label Echinochloa sp.

comparisons.key_distinctions: NO ligule helps distinguish Echinochloa from Digitaria ciliaris and Panicum capillare, but NOT E. crus-galli from E. muricata/colona/walteri. Species-level E. crus-galli is supported by a mature fertile lemma with abruptly delimited thin tip and tiny hairline; E. muricata lacks that demarcation. E. colona generally has smaller, less bristly short panicle branches; E. walteri has often hairy leaf sheaths. These alone are insufficient for assured species calls.

detailed_pairs.look_here_first: Also has NO true ligule and may have a near-identical panicle with variable awns. Some differences in rachis bristles or spikelet hairs are only suggestive and unreliable across populations. CONFIRM several fully mature florets at ~25–40×: E. crus-galli upper fertile lemma has a hardened body that ends abruptly at a thin membranous tip, divided by a tiny line of hairs; E. muricata lacks this sharp demarcation and hair line. Compare the palea tip too.
detailed_pairs.warning: Avoid a native-vs-introduced decision from one seedhead photograph. Local range claims for E. muricata not established in this pass.

detailed_pairs.look_here_first: Also without ligule, but typically smaller/less bristly short-branch panicles, often several short racemes, smaller ~2–3 mm awnless spikelets, and sometimes purplish banding on blades. These clues overlap; check mature anatomy.
detailed_pairs.warning: Color bands and awn absence are not stand-alone identifications.

detailed_pairs.look_here_first: Wetland species also lacking a ligule; much hairier coarse basal leaf sheaths and long awns are useful clues, but confirm mature fertile lemma (no E. crus-galli-type line of hairs beneath the tip).
detailed_pairs.warning: Hairiness varies and does not certify a species. Verify occurrence separately.

detailed_pairs.look_here_first: Thin, extremely open floating/tumbling panicle and true ligule of hairs, unlike typically stout relatively densely clustered Echinochloa branches and absent ligule.
detailed_pairs.warning: Do not conflate with genus Digitaria cognata, commonly called fall witchgrass.

detailed_pairs.look_here_first: Several nearly fingerlike one-sided racemes with paired spikelets, and a definite MEMBRANOUS ligule at the leaf collar.
detailed_pairs.warning: Both are disturbed-site warm-season grasses; head silhouette alone is insufficient.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Barnyardgrass — absent ligule → branching panicle → mature fertile lemma test
steps: START with PHYSICALLY ARCHIVED panel 1: the lifted Australian flowering tuft shows attached culms and branching heads with a partly obscured soil/root mass, NOT a fully cleaned root system or Texas voucher. Compare the archived panicle and crowded spikelets in panel 3.

OPEN THE TRUE INNER COLLAR: physically archived Harry Rose panel 2 actually demonstrates ABSENCE of both a projecting membrane and a hair-fringe ligule at the blade–sheath junction. Its original source was Commons but the JPEG is NOW STORED LOCALLY. The visible seam is not a tiny ligule. Native E. muricata also lacks a ligule.

CHECK the crowded flowering branches (panel 3), then an external awn-bearing reference (panel 4). Published lower sterile lemma awns can vary from 0 to about 50 mm; awn length and panicle color alone cannot distinguish E. crus-galli from native E. muricata.

OPEN PHYSICALLY ARCHIVED panels 5 and 6: panel 5 has the photographer's actual spikelet anatomy labels; panel 6 shows two mature spikelets and three existing gross arrows. These are NOT merely external links. Separate lower and upper glumes and the sterile and fertile lemmas at 10–20× with a 1-mm scale; present photos do not prove veins or the microscopic fertile-lemma tip.

CRITICAL 25–40× UPPER FERTILE LEMMA TEST (not glumes): inspect the hard fertile lemma body, abruptly delimited thin terminal margin and transverse tiny hairline described for E. crus-galli. Native E. muricata has a more gradual tip transition and lacks the continuous line. Compare multiple ripe voucher-identified specimens with a 0.5–1 mm bar. Existing panel 6 does NOT prove this separation; otherwise record Echinochloa sp.

NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: connected Texas rooted annual, opened inner collar with 1-mm reference, 2.5–4 mm mature spikelet with lower glume ~0.8–1.7 mm and upper glume ~3–4 mm separately measured, lower sterile lemma awn insertion, and paired E. crus-galli/E. muricata UPPER fertile lemma apices at 25–40×. NEEDS_SITE_QA: five physical and three remote target images, one external other-species panel, ten gross arrows, exact individual CC rights and mobile page display.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: A species-name image from Commons is a taxon-labelled reference, not independent anatomical verification; use microscope for close E. crus-galli / E. muricata calls.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Five genuine target-species JPEGs are now physically archived, including a true absent-ligule collar, two reproductive macro views and a connected lifted flowering tuft. The Australian source photos are not Texas vouchers and no image independently resolves the critical E. muricata fertile-lemma tip comparison.

Confirm a mature fertile upper lemma with abruptly membranous tip and line of minute hairs under ~25× before naming a closely similar species.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: BARNYARDGRASS: open an attached blade–sheath collar and confirm NO ligule or auricles; follow a coarse annual branched panicle to a mature 2.5–4 mm spikelet. To separate E. crus-galli from native E. muricata, dissect several ripe upper fertile lemmas for an abruptly thin tip and a transverse line of minute hairs; a seedhead alone is insufficient.

measured_key.growth: Warm-season annual, culms often 20–150 cm; erect to ascending from a decumbent base, no diagnostic persistent rhizomes. Sheaths usually smooth, occasionally hairy.
measured_key.ligule_collar: Ligule absent (0 mm): neither projecting membrane nor true hair fringe; auricles absent. Nearby sheath or node hairs are not a ligule.
measured_key.panicle: Branched terminal panicle often 6–22 cm; side branches about 2–10 cm, spikelets clustered and rachis sometimes bristly.
measured_key.spikelet: Usually 2.5–4 mm (regional descriptions extend to 5 mm), dorsally compressed, with LOWER sterile floret and UPPER fertile floret. Awn excluded from length.
measured_key.lower_glume: About 0.8–1.7 mm across sources, roughly one-third to two-fifths spikelet length; clasping base, 3–5-veined.
measured_key.upper_glume: About 3–4 mm, near spikelet length, generally 5-veined; rough or bristly along veins, sometimes with minute point.
measured_key.lower_sterile_lemma: About 3–4 mm, 5–7-veined; terminal awn absent to approximately 50 mm. The long variable awn belongs to THIS lemma, not the upper fertile lemma.
measured_key.upper_fertile_lemma: About 2–3.5 mm, hard shiny body, 5-veined, with abruptly delimited thin withering tip and tiny transverse hairline; palea hard, tip sometimes reflexed. Examine ripe organs under 25–40×.
measured_key.awns: Upper fertile lemma without a long awn. Lower sterile lemma may be awnless or have a 0–50 mm awn; awn presence, color and panicle bristles cannot diagnose species.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.lookalikes: Native E. muricata also lacks a ligule and may have nearly identical panicle and awn variability: mature fertile lemma-tip boundary and minute hairline are needed for confident separation. E. colona usually smaller, shorter branches and smaller often awnless spikelets but shares absent ligule. E. walteri can have hairy sheaths. Panicum capillare has a hair-fringe ligule; Digitaria ciliaris a true membranous ligule and fingerlike racemes.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.measurement_caveat: GrassBase: 0.8–1.4 mm lower glume, 3–4 mm spikelet; USDA IDtools: 1.2–1.7 mm lower glume, 3–5 mm spikelet. These are reference ranges, not rigid thresholds.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.short: A true ABSENT ligule, then a crowded branched panicle
field_id_short_tiles.details: Open an intact inner blade–sheath junction: Echinochloa has no projecting membrane or ligule hair fringe (0 mm), and no auricles. The physically archived Harry Rose collar image is panel 2 and demonstrates this negative character; panel 3 shows the crowded branched head. A few nearby sheath hairs are not a ligule. E. muricata shares this character, so the collar alone does not settle introduced versus native identity.
field_id_short_tiles.status: COLLAR IMAGE PRESENT; TEXAS SAME-PLANT CALIBRATION NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · CHECK GROWTH & FLOWERING BRANCHES
field_id_short_tiles.details: Look for a fibrous-rooted annual, often 30–200 cm tall in Flora of North America, with a branched 5–25 cm terminal panicle and roughly 1.5–10 cm lateral branches. Physically archived Harry Rose panel 1 NOW shows a lifted tuft with multiple attached flowering heads, converging leafy culms and a partly obscured adhering root/soil mass, with three pixel-verified broad arrows. It is Australian, not a Texas voucher; it does not expose a cleaned complete root system. Panel 3 shows the crowded flowering branches; panel 7 is an external seedling reference.
field_id_short_tiles.status: ACTUAL CONNECTED LIFTED TUFT PHOTO — FULL ROOTS AND TEXAS VOUCHER MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE ONE SPIKELET AND ITS GLUMES
field_id_short_tiles.short: 2.5–4 mm, two florets; lower glume shorter
field_id_short_tiles.details: At 10–20× isolate a mature spikelet about 2.5–4 mm long (excluding any awn), with a LOWER sterile and an UPPER fertile floret, not two separate spikelets. Lower glume is roughly 0.8–1.7 mm and usually 3–5-veined; upper glume is near full spikelet length, commonly 3–4 mm and 5-veined. Panel 5 is the photographer's annotated real spikelet and panel 6 shows two mature source-identified spikelets with three arrows to actual gross structures; neither is a measured Texas dissection proving glume venation or the diagnostic fertile-lemma apex.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL ANNOTATED + MATURE SPIKELET PHOTOS; CALIBRATED GLUMES STILL MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · FIND THE ACTUAL LEMMA AWN
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower sterile lemma awn 0–50 mm; fertile lemma hard
field_id_short_tiles.details: The lower sterile lemma is often approximately 3–4 mm and may be AWNLESS or carry a long terminal awn to about 50 mm, even varying along one panicle. The upper fertile lemma is about 2–3.5 mm with a hardened glossy body, and does NOT bear that long awn. Do not label a bristle on the flowering rachis as a lemma awn.
field_id_short_tiles.status: AWN VARIATION VISIBLE; INSERTION/MEASUREMENT PHOTO GAP

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · NATIVE LOOK-ALIKE WARNING
field_id_short_tiles.short: E. muricata ALSO has no ligule
field_id_short_tiles.details: Native rough barnyardgrass (E. muricata) can share the absent ligule, similar panicle and variable awns. For a confident E. crus-galli determination, dissect several ripe UPPER fertile lemmas at about 25–40×: the hard body ends abruptly at a thin withering tip separated by a transverse line of minute hairs. The current gallery does NOT independently resolve that line; otherwise record Echinochloa sp., not a native-versus-introduced verdict.
field_id_short_tiles.status: CRITICAL NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — MATCHED MATURE LEMMA TIPS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · SPLIT OTHER LOCAL LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Junglerice, witchgrass and crabgrass need collar checks
field_id_short_tiles.details: Native E. muricata and introduced E. colona can also lack a ligule. Panicum capillare has a HAIR-FRINGE ligule and airy open panicle; Digitaria ciliaris has a MEMBRANOUS ligule and fingerlike racemes. Panel 8 is the DIFFERENT-SPECIES southern crabgrass seedhead, not a photographed crabgrass collar. Panel 2 is the actual Echinochloa absent-ligule photo; panel 3 shows the target head. For E. crus-galli versus E. muricata, dissect mature upper fertile lemma tips at 25–40× and inspect the minute transverse hairline; stop at Echinochloa sp. if unresolved.
field_id_short_tiles.status: COMPARISON LESSON; PUBLIC PHOTO + SITE QA GAPS
